Subsequently, Public Works Department leased it out for 3 years. The plaintiffs then filed an application before the Ministry of Public Works for lease of the suit land in their favour on receipt of compensation money back. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 submitted a report as called for stating that the departmental manufacturing of bricks was closed due to Government policy and there is no Government plan for the use of the land further and before the return of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs the lease of land was granted by public Works Department for three years should have been cancelled. The plaintiffs also submitted that written representation to the Ministry of Land administration and Land Reforms for early return of the suit land in their favour. The Government decided to return the suit land and similar other land in favour of the original owners and issued urgent Instructions vide memo dated 03.07.1993 for taking steps for that purpose but inspite of that decision the plaintiffs came to know on 17.04.1994 that the suit land is in the process of being handed over to a 3rd party with a view to deprive the plain-tiffs from their rightful claim and hence the suit for decree of mandatory injunction directing the defendants to formally release the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs on receipts of compensation money back and for a decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendants from transferring the suit land to any 3rd party was filed. 

 4. The senior Assistant Judge, Sylhet Sadar, Sylhet after perusing the materials on record, examining the witnesses and hearing the parties, decreed the suit. On an appeal filed by the defendants being Title Appeal No. 221 of 1996 the lower appellate Court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of affirmance by the lower appellate Court, the government as petitioner filed Civil Revision before the High court Division which was discharged. 

 8. In developing his argument the learned Additional Attorney General further submits that the suit land having been acquired on 01.12.1966 by the Public Works Department for the purpose of manufacture of brick therein vide L.A Case No. 15/66-67 and possession was given to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and bricks have been manufactured in the said land for some years, the High Court Division erred in law in discharging the rule as well as the court below erred in law in decreeing the suit. 

 13. The original suit filed by the plain-tiffs was for a decree of mandatory injunction directing the defendants (government) to formally release the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs on receipt of the compensation money back and also for a decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendant from transferring the suit land to any third party.
